title: Changeset
description: Describes one user-visible outcome, classified from a consumer's perspective. Supersedes changeset@2 — the summary has no length cap and may be layered, and disposition lets the producer update an existing entry or recommend none. Produced by courier's changeset-analyzer, consumed by courier's release-summarizer and by sentinel.

summary.description: The changelog entry, in Markdown. Start with a lead line that states what the reader can now do or what changed for them. Add bullets, sub-bullets or audience sections (what you see, scripting, upgrading) only when there is more the reader needs: why it helps, where it appears, what to do, and any limit they will hit. A one-line entry is correct when that is all there is. No length cap; detail follows what the reader needs. When disposition is none, state why no entry is needed.

disposition.description: new: a new entry for one user-visible outcome. update-existing: this change belongs to an outcome that already has an unreleased entry, named in updates. none: nothing a consumer sees, or it fixes something not yet released; no entry is needed.

updates.description: Path or identifier of the existing unreleased changeset this change extends. Required when disposition is update-existing.

consumer_impact.description: Whether this change is observable to someone outside this repo. See shared/references/delivery/changesets.md for classification rules.

semver_impact.description: Version bump this change requires, per the Semver table in shared/references/delivery/changesets.md. release-summarizer takes max(semver_impact) across a release's changesets rather than re-deriving it.

files_changed.description: Paths of files added, modified, or deleted

tests_added.description: Paths of test files added or modified

acceptance_criteria_met.description: IDs from spec@1.acceptance_criteria that this changeset satisfies, or ["unlinked"] when no spec is linked

criteria_evidence.description: Per-criterion evidence trail: exactly where each acceptance_criteria_met ID is tested and implemented. When sourced from implementer's own build, test_line and implementation_line are exact. When reconstructed from a diff with no smith run behind it, file-level entries without line numbers are acceptable rather than fabricating precision that was never observed. A criterion may have more than one entry when it is proven in more than one place.

breaking_changes.description: Public API or behavior changes that break existing callers. Each entry states old behavior, new behavior, and what the caller does about it.

commits.description: Git SHAs of commits in this changeset

linked_requirement.description: ID of the requirement@1 this change ultimately traces back to. Propagated from spec@1.linked_requirement via plan@1.linked_requirement when available.

reasoning.description: Agent scratchpad — not consumed downstream. A limit or action a reader needs belongs in summary, not here.
